verdict.rationale: Apple documents a Neural Engine in the M4 family and ships official ML tooling today: MLX from Apple machine learning research, plus Metal 4 and PyTorch backends for on-device ML acceleration. However, the pack gives no TOPS figure or stated precision for the Neural Engine, only relative claims like "over 3x faster than M1 Max". None of the cited SDKs is documented as targeting the Neural Engine itself; they target Apple silicon and the GPU. Missing for 10: a published TOPS figure with stated precision (e.g., INT8/FP16), evidence of a Neural Engine–specific SDK or runtime (e.g., Core ML), and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, the chip's AI acceleration is exposed to developers — an NPU or neural engine with a published TOPS figure (precision stated) and an official SDK or runtime that ships today

citations.quote: a Neural Engine that is over 3x faster than M1 Max, Mac Studio with M4 Max can run on-device AI models incredibly fast
MLX is an array framework for machine learning on Apple silicon, brought to you by Apple machine learning research.
Accelerate the training of machine learning models in third-party frameworks right on your Mac with PyTorch backends.
It supports Metal 4 and GPU Neural Accelerators for maximum performance
